onWatch 2.14.15 fixes the 7-day and 30-day usage charts, which drew every provider's history as a broken, dotted line in 2.14.14.

## Fixes

- **7d and 30d charts are continuous again.** Since 2.14.14, long ranges are sampled to about 200 points so they load fast. The chart's gap detection still expected one point per poll, so every segment was drawn as a faded dashed "no data" gap with a dot at each end. The gap threshold now follows the spacing of the data on screen. Real gaps, such as hours when the mach

`onwatch update`, or re-run the installer. The cycle cleanup and a new database index run once on first start and take about a second on a large database.
- Menubar snapshots are built in the background shortly after each poll, so opening the popover never waits on the database.
- Database work was cut sharply: index seeks instead of full-table scans, batched value loads instead of one query per snapshot, and chart ranges sampled in SQL.

onWatch 2.14.13 brings the Windows tray up to the macOS menubar: a native quick view, a sharp tray icon, and start at login with restart after a crash.

## Windows: native quick view

The quick view used to open as a Microsoft Edge app window, with a title bar, a taskbar button, a fixed 360x680 size and a cold browser start on every click. It now opens as a borderless WebView2 popup anchored next to the tray:

- It fits its content and scales with each monitor's DPI.
- It has rounded corners on Windows 11 a
- An explicit `--db` or absolute database path is kept as given instead of being redirected.
